question: In which year was the climate classification first published in Russian as ‘thermal zones of the earth’?
solution:
The correct answer is **__1884__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Köppen climate classification** system was developed by **German botanist-climatologist Wladimir Köppen**. His system was **first published in 1884**, with **modifications in 1918 and 1936**.
 
• In 1884 **Thermal Zones of the earth** was published in **Russian**.
 
• This classification system is one of the most widely used for identifying and defining climate zones throughout the world.
 
• It defines climatic boundaries in accordance with mapped vegetation zones (biomes), largely basing it on local vegetation, which is a reflection of climate over time.
 
• The system comprehensively categorizes climates into five main types - A: Tropical, B: Dry, C: Temperate, D: Continental, E: Polar. These main types are further divided based on seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is a basic table structure outlining the five main climate groups recognized by Köppen's system:

 
 

 Main Group
 Designation
 Conditions
 
 

 Tropical
 A
 High temperatures year-round, significant annual rainfall
 
 

 Dry
 B
 Limited rainfall making it hostile for plant life; further divided into arid (BW, desert climate) and semiarid (BS, steppe climate)
 
 

 Temperate
 Mild/Moderate(C)
 Experiences warm, humid summers and mild to cool winters
 
 

 Continental (Cold)
 D
 Severe winters, and often severe summers, typically with snowfall in winter
 
 

 Polar
 E
 Very cold and dry all year
